documents.title: Office Visit - Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six-month check. No skin lesions since early last year. GI: normal bowels, strict gluten-free at home, the odd slip at restaurants. Joints: some days her fingers ache by evening, nothing swollen. Mouth sores occasionally.

Meds: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID, ferrous sulfate 325 mg TID, folic acid 1 mg, vitamin D3 2000 IU. NKDA.

Exam: weight 57 kg. Mouth without ulcers. Skin clear. Hands without synovitis. Heart and lungs normal.

A/P: celiac/DH quiet; tTG today. Iron deficiency: CBC and ferritin today. SLE on hydroxychloroquine; rheumatology due in the fall. Return in 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your hemoglobin is 12.2 now, in the normal range for the first time since 2020, and ferritin 35. The celiac antibody is negative, which means the diet is working. White count 3.8, a hair low, which is a lupus thing and rheumatology keeps an eye on it. Stay on the iron for now.

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Yay!! Thank you. Can I drop the iron to once a day? Three times a day is a lot to remember.

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Let's keep three times a day until your stores are a bit fuller; we'll talk about cutting back at your fall visit.

documents.title: Office Visit - Joint Pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
31F with SLE and celiac disease, here for the follow-up she pushed from July.

S: over the last three months her joints have ached on and off all over, but mostly the hands. Fingers are sore today. When I asked about mouth sores, she remembered a painful one a few months back that took about a week and a half to heal by itself. No fever, no rash, no chest pain or breathlessness. Skin and bowels fine.
New family detail today: her father had a bout of subacute thyroiditis some years ago; it settled. He also has type 2 diabetes. Mother lupus, maternal grandmother RA, paternal aunt celiac, as before.

Meds: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID, ferrous sulfate 325 mg TID, folic acid 1 mg, vitamin D3 2000 IU. NKDA.

O: vitals normal. Mouth: no ulcer now. Fingers mildly tender over the small joints, no swelling or warmth; wrists full range. Skin without rash or alopecia patches. Heart and lungs normal.

A/P
1. SLE with ongoing arthralgia and an oral ulcer: adding an anti-Sm antibody to round out her serologies, and CBC. Continue hydroxychloroquine. Will send a note to rheumatology to see her sooner than her yearly slot.
2. Recurrent aphthous ulcers vs lupus ulcer: both possible; self-limited.
3. Celiac/DH, iron deficiency: stable.
4. Flu and updated COVID vaccines today.

documents.title: Note to Rheumatology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Faxed today's note to her rheumatology office asking for an earlier follow-up: three months of hand-predominant arthralgia, a recent oral ulcer, on hydroxychloroquine 400 mg/day. Anti-Sm pending, will forward.

documents.title: Test result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Zoe, the anti-Sm antibody came back positive. It is another antibody that goes along with lupus, it confirms the diagnosis you already have and does not by itself change treatment. Your blood count is fine. I sent it to rheumatology; their office should call you with an earlier appointment.

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Rheumatology office note from visit October 25, 2023, seen early at PCP's request.

Hand-predominant joint aches over the summer, one oral ulcer that healed. Today: no synovitis, no rash. Recent anti-Sm positive, noted; adds to her serologic profile without changing management.

Plan: continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily. Labs at her next yearly visit. Call for any swelling, rash, chest pain or urine changes.

Rheumatology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32 yo yearly visit. Busy at work, feels well. Joints have been calmer since the fall. No skin flares. Gluten-free. Mouth ulcers rare.
Meds: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg three times daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. NKDA.
Social: never smoker, minimal alcohol.

Exam: vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. Skin clear. Joints normal. No edema.

A/P
- Health maintenance: Pap/HPV current (2022). PHQ-2 0. Flu and COVID in the fall.
- SLE: CBC, CMP, UA today for rheumatology's records.
- Iron deficiency: ferritin today.
- Celiac/DH: quiet.
Return in a year.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All of this week's labs look good: blood count, kidney and liver tests, and urine normal, ferritin holding steady. Copies sent to rheumatology.

events.reason: Fatigue, shortness of breath, dark urine, yellow eyes

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED physician record, visit Sunday October 6, 2024. Faxed to PCP.

HPI: 32-year-old woman with SLE and celiac disease. Three weeks of increasing tiredness and getting winded with stairs, dark tea-colored urine for about a week, and a coworker noticed her eyes looked yellow. She is on hydroxychloroquine but no immunosuppressive therapy. No fever, chest pain, bleeding or new medications.
Meds: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID, ferrous sulfate 325 mg TID, folic acid 1 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: tired-appearing, alert. Scleral icterus. Lungs clear, heart regular with no murmur. Abdomen soft; spleen tip felt, mild splenomegaly. No rash, no lymphadenopathy.

Results: hemoglobin 8.2 g/dL. Reticulocytes 8.1%. Total bilirubin 4.5 mg/dL, direct 0.5. LDH 612 U/L. Haptoglobin undetectable. Direct antiglobulin test positive. Smear: spherocytes. Creatinine normal. Urine hCG negative.

ED course: hemodynamically stable, symptoms improved with rest; repeat hemoglobin unchanged. Discussed with on-call hematology, who will see her in clinic in two days.

Impression: autoimmune hemolytic anemia, DAT positive, in a patient with SLE.
Disposition: discharged home. Return for chest pain, fainting, worsening breathlessness or rapidly darkening urine. Hematology clinic Tuesday. PCP follow-up this week.

documents.title: ED Follow-up Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED record received this morning. Called Zoe: still tired, no worse, urine a bit lighter today. Hematology tomorrow confirmed. Booked with PCP Thursday. Reviewed reasons to go back to the ED.

documents.title: Hematology Consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Outside hematology/oncology clinic, new consultation October 8, 2024, sent from the ED. Copy to PCP and rheumatology.

Summary: SLE since 2021 on hydroxychloroquine, celiac disease with dermatitis herpetiformis, past iron deficiency. Presented to the ED two days ago with three weeks of fatigue, exertional breathlessness, dark urine and icterus; hemoglobin 8.2, reticulocytes 8.1%, indirect hyperbilirubinemia, LDH elevated, haptoglobin undetectable, polyspecific DAT positive, spherocytes on smear.
Meds: hydroxychloroquine, ferrous sulfate, folic acid, vitamin D3. NKDA.

Exam: mild icterus. Otherwise as per ED.

Workup here: monospecific DAT C3d positive, IgG negative. Cold agglutinin titer 1:512. Hepatitis B surface antigen nonreactive.

Assessment: cold autoimmune hemolytic anemia, secondary to SLE.

Plan:
1. Rituximab 375 mg/m2 (600 mg) IV weekly for four doses starting October 15 in our infusion suite. Premedication per protocol.
2. Keep warm: gloves outdoors, avoid cold drinks and cold rooms; warm IV fluids and blood if ever transfused.
3. Continue folic acid 1 mg daily.
4. CBC with retic weekly during treatment. Transfuse for hemoglobin under 7 or symptoms.

Hematology

documents.title: Office Visit - Post ED
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after the ED on Sunday and hematology on Tuesday. Hematology diagnosed cold autoimmune hemolytic anemia related to her lupus (C3d-positive DAT, cold agglutinin titer 1:512) and plans rituximab weekly x4 starting next Tuesday.

S: still tired, can do her work from home, winded on the stairs. Urine lighter. Eyes less yellow per her. No chest pain, no fainting.
Meds: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID, ferrous sulfate 325 mg TID, folic acid 1 mg, vitamin D3 2000 IU. NKDA.

O: vitals as charted. Mild scleral icterus. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P
1. Cold AIHA secondary to SLE: hemoglobin 8.6 today. Plan per hematology. Reviewed cold avoidance, especially with winter coming.
2. Vaccines: flu and COVID today, ahead of rituximab, which blunts response for months afterward.
3. Iron: hemolysis is not iron loss; hematology fine with continuing for now, ferritin next time.
Will follow her hematology letters; see me in the spring or sooner.

documents.title: Patient Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Zoe called after her second rituximab infusion asking whether she can go to a friend's outdoor birthday this weekend. Advised layers, gloves and a hat, warm drinks, and to head indoors if her fingers or toes go numb or her urine darkens. Next infusion next Tuesday. No new symptoms.

documents.title: Hematology Treatment Summary
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Hematology infusion summary. Rituximab 600 mg IV given October 15, 22, 29 and November 5, 2024, all four doses without infusion reaction.
Hemoglobin trend: 8.4, 8.9, 9.6, and 10.1 on November 5. Icterus resolved. Patient keeping warm, feels better.
Plan: CBC with retic monthly; clinic visit in about 10 weeks. Continue folic acid.

Hematology

documents.author: hematology

Cold AIHA secondary to SLE, after four doses of rituximab completed in November. She feels close to normal; managing the cold with layers and gloves.
Today: hemoglobin 11.6, reticulocytes 1.8%, bilirubin normal.
Assessment: in remission after rituximab.
Plan: observe. CBC every 3 months through her PCP or here; clinic in 6 months. Call with dark urine, yellowing or new fatigue.

Hematology

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, hematology/oncology service. Admitted September 28, discharged October 1, 2025. Sent to PCP.

Reason for admission: recurrent hemolysis needing transfusion.

History: 33-year-old with SLE and cold autoimmune hemolytic anemia treated with rituximab in fall 2024. A month of gradually worsening fatigue and mild jaundice, then a sharp drop in energy the last few days. Home medications: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily (she takes it, it was missing from the intake list), ferrous sulfate 325 mg three times daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. NKDA.

Exam on admission: mild scleral icterus. No hepatosplenomegaly. Heart and lungs normal.

Data: hemoglobin 8.2, reticulocytes 8%, total bilirubin 3.4 with direct 0.4. Polyspecific DAT positive; monospecific IgG positive and C3d positive. Urinalysis negative for hemoglobin. Smear with spherocytes, no schistocytes.

Hospital course: one unit of packed red cells through a blood warmer on the first evening, tolerated. IgG now positive alongside the known complement pattern: warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia, mixed with her cold disease. Started prednisone 60 mg daily (about 1 mg/kg). Hemoglobin 9.0 on the morning of discharge, bilirubin falling.

Discharge diagnoses: warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (mixed type with known cold AIHA); SLE; celiac disease.
Discharge medications: prednisone 60 mg daily (new); hydroxychloroquine, ferrous sulfate, folic acid, vitamin D3 unchanged.
Follow-up: hematology clinic in about 3 weeks, taper to be directed there. PCP within a week.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Discharge summary received. Called within two business days of discharge. She is home, tired but better than before admission. Has prednisone 60 mg and is taking it with breakfast. Understands the hematology follow-up. No fever, no dark urine. Visit booked with PCP Monday.

documents.title: Office Visit - Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 5 days after discharge. Admitted 9/28 to 10/1 for recurrent hemolysis: hemoglobin 8.2, DAT now IgG and C3d positive, one unit of blood, started prednisone 60 mg daily. Hospital team calls it warm AIHA on top of her cold disease.

S: more energy since the transfusion. Sleeping poorly on the prednisone, hungry all the time. Urine normal color. No fever, no infections.
Meds reconciled: prednisone 60 mg daily (new), hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID, ferrous sulfate 325 mg TID, folic acid 1 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. NKDA.

O: vitals as charted. Faint icterus. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema.

A/P
1. Warm AIHA, mixed with cold AIHA, secondary to SLE: hemoglobin 9.4 today, improving. Prednisone per hematology; taper there. Problem list updated.
2. Steroid side effects: glucose today. Take in the morning with food. Sleep hygiene.
3. Flu vaccine today.
4. SLE: rheumatology copied on the summary.
Return in about 2 to 3 months, sooner if any dark urine.

medications.sig: Take 4 tablets (40 mg) by mouth daily

documents.author: PCP

Year-end visit. Hematology tapering her prednisone: now 10 mg daily since mid-December, hemoglobin 11.9 there.

S: feeling like herself, sleeping better at the lower dose. Up a couple of kilos with the steroid appetite. No dark urine, no yellowing. Keeps warm. Joints fine, no rash, gut fine.
Meds: prednisone 10 mg daily (hematology taper), hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg three times daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. NKDA.

O: vitals as charted, weight 59.5 kg. No icterus. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, no spleen felt. Skin clear, mouth clear.

A/P
1. Warm and cold AIHA secondary to SLE: hemoglobin 12.0 today. Taper per hematology. CBC again in about 3 months, order placed.
2. Immune suppression with steroids and recent rituximab: PCV20 today.
3. SLE: rheumatology in the spring.
4. Celiac/DH, iron deficiency: stable on current regimen.
Annual physical later in the year.

documents.title: Yesterday's labs

documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Eye clinic, exam March 10, 2026. Five years of hydroxychloroquine; yearly retinal screening now begins.
Acuity 20/20 both eyes. Fundi normal. 10-2 visual fields full. SD-OCT macula normal, no parafoveal thinning. Fundus autofluorescence normal.
Impression: no hydroxychloroquine retinopathy. Repeat in one year.

Plan: continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily; eye screening up to date. See in 6 months.
